tagline: A rapidly developing Asian side district with ferry connections to the Princes' Islands and a growing food and café scene.

items.name: İskele Café Kartal
items.description: Right at the ferry terminal with views of the Sea of Marmara and the Princes' Islands on clear days. Simple and pleasant.

items.name: Ritim İstanbul AVM Cafés
items.description: Multiple café options inside the modern Ritim shopping mall — a reliable stop for coffee and a break.

items.name: Kartal Sahil Balık Restoranları
items.description: A cluster of fish restaurants along the Kartal waterfront. Fresh, local seafood with views of the Princes' Islands.

items.name: Merkez Restoranları
items.description: The streets around Kartal's centre have a good range of local Turkish restaurants — pide, köfte, and traditional dishes at very reasonable prices.

items.name: Ferry to Princes' Islands
items.description: Kartal's main draw — a frequent ferry service to the Princes' Islands (Buyukada, Heybeliada). One of Istanbul's best day trips.
items.tip: Ferries run frequently, especially on weekends. Go on a weekday to avoid the crowds on the islands.

items.name: Kartal Sahili
items.description: A pleasant waterfront promenade with views of the islands and mountains on clear days. Good for an evening walk.

tips: Kartal is on the M4 metro line — direct connection to Kadıköy and Sabiha Gökçen Airport, plus a Marmaray station.
The main reason to come is the ferry to the Princes' Islands — one of Istanbul's greatest day trips.
The waterfront is pleasant but the neighbourhood itself is primarily residential and commercial.
Maltepe (the next stop west on the metro) has a more developed waterfront and café scene.
